title: What kind of four-sided figure is ABYX when XY is level?
description: When X and Y are at the same distance from A and B, the length XY is compared with AB and the shape ABYX is named from its sides and angles. Keeko's doubt is that ABYX is a square because the top side equals the base.
teaching_notes: One idea: ABYX has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so it is a rectangle, and it is a square only when all four sides match. Watch for students who call it a square just because the top side equals the base.

source: In each of these cases (X and Y at the same distance from A
video_script.why: A learner compares XY with AB and names the shape ABYX when X and Y are at equal distances from A and B.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with AB seven centimetres, and the four-sided figure formed when X and Y are level
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with a level line XY cutting off a smaller four-sided figure ABYX at the bottom
video_script.wrong_answer: the four-sided figure is a square, because the top side equals the base
video_script.wrong_move: calls ABYX a square because XY equals AB, without checking the other two sides
video_script.payoff_line: Ex why is as long as eigh bee, and the figure is a rectangle.

final_answer.value: XY = AB; ABYX is a rectangle

maths_rules: X and Y at equal distances from A and B: XY = AB = 7 cm
angle A = angle B = 90°; XY is level with AB, so angle X = angle Y = 90°
AX = BY (the same distance up), and AB = XY
four right angles and equal opposite sides: ABYX is a rectangle
AX and BY are at most 4 cm, so they never equal AB = 7 cm: ABYX is not a square
video_script.design: The level line is drawn, then ABYX is checked for its lengths and its angles, then named.
